meta.rule: no finding rests on a screenshot alone; each carries a source citation or a measured number
meta.stage_note: Stage 1 was read-only until the owner authorised fixing the auth outage (F-01) because the authenticated product could not be audited while sign-in was impossible. F-15 and F-17 were then also directed by the owner.

landing_1440.title: Clarion — Study Workspace, Assignment Workflow & Style Coaching

findings.title: CSP had no frame-src, so Turnstile was blocked and NOBODY could sign up or sign in
findings.symptom: Signup: the captcha never rendered (0 iframes), the hidden cf-turnstile-response input stayed empty, and 'Create account' was permanently disabled. Sign-in: the button was NOT gated on the token, so a user typed their password, clicked Sign In, and got back 403 'Security check required — complete the captcha and try again' — about a captcha that was not on screen and could not be.
findings.cause: server/security.py:538-547 built the CSP with default-src/script-src/style-src/font-src/img-src/media-src/connect-src/frame-ancestors and never emitted frame-src. The docstring at :526 had described frame-src and worker-src as part of this policy since the Turnstile work; neither was ever in the header. With no frame-src, default-src 'self' governed frames.
findings.history: Not a fresh regression. Before commit 9b692ac the policy was script-src 'self', which blocked the Turnstile script outright. 9b692ac opened script-src and connect-src for Cloudflare but missed the third directive, so the symptom changed rather than cleared.
findings.evidence_before: curl -sI returned a CSP with no frame-src. Console on every auth surface: "Framing 'https://challenges.cloudflare.com/' violates ... default-src 'self'". Measured: signup button disabled:true with all fields valid; POST /api/login with an empty token -> 403.
findings.evidence_after: frame-src present in the live header; Turnstile mints a 730-char token in ~6-12s; a real account (qadesign1) was created end to end through the UI with no bypass header.
findings.cost: Total acquisition and re-entry outage — every new signup and every returning sign-in.
findings.fix: Added frame-src https://challenges.cloudflare.com https://*.challenges.cloudflare.com and worker-src 'self' blob: data: to the CSP. frame-ancestors 'none' untouched; no gate weakened.
findings.note: This was NOT in the brief's defect list and outranked everything that was.

findings.title: One undefined font token made the entire signed-in app render in the OS system font
findings.symptom: Owner: 'i hate the fonts in helpotron, it looks ass'. Measured cause: five different first-choice font families on a single screen.
findings.cause: web/src/App.jsx:709 puts Tailwind's `font-sans` utility on the root .app-canvas div. --font-sans was never defined in the @theme inline block in web/src/index.css, so `font-sans` resolved to Tailwind's default OS stack and overrode the "Inter Variable" set on <body> for the whole application. Only components that explicitly named a font-* token (font-body-md, font-headline-lg, ...) escaped it.
findings.evidence: Ancestor walk from a mis-rendered heading: the font boundary is exactly div.app-canvas (computed first family -apple-system) whose parent main#root computes Inter Variable. Family census on the dashboard: -apple-system x10, Inter Variable x10, ui-monospace x2, Hanken Grotesk Variable x1, JetBrains Mono Variable x2.
findings.not_the_cause: The typefaces load correctly. @fontsource-variable/{inter,hanken-grotesk,jetbrains-mono} are installed, imported at web/src/main.jsx:4-6, shipped as woff2 in the build, and all three report status 'loaded'. The problem was never the font choice.
findings.fix: Defined --font-sans (Inter Variable) and --font-mono (JetBrains Mono Variable) in the @theme block. Verified in the built CSS: .font-sans{font-family:Inter Variable,...}.
findings.remaining: The type SCALE is still incoherent — see F-16. Fixing the family is necessary but not sufficient.

findings.title: Type hierarchy is inverted — the dashboard h1 is smaller than body text
findings.symptom: The authenticated dashboard's <h1> ('Dashboard') renders at 14px/600 while body copy renders at 16px/400. A 32px Hanken Grotesk h2 ('Your subjects') sits below it, so the visual hierarchy contradicts the document hierarchy.
findings.evidence: Measured on the authenticated dashboard at 1440. Also: '0 assignments present' is set in JetBrains Mono 12px — a monospace face used for prose, not data.
findings.cost: Screen readers and search engines get one outline; sighted users get a different one. The page's real title is the smallest text on it.
findings.fix: Decide one scale in docs/design/DIRECTION.md and apply it: h1 is the page title at display size, h2 sections below it, mono reserved for numerals and identifiers.

findings.owner_reaction: Owner, looking at the live site mid-audit: 'why does the site look broken'. Verified it was NOT caused by any deploy of mine — a clean signed-out context measured h1 left=0 and hero padding 0px/0px, identical to the 19:27 baseline taken before the first change. All 9 referenced assets returned 200.
findings.fix_applied: Declared --spacing-container-padding: clamp(1rem, 3vw, 2.5rem) in the @theme block, alongside the --spacing-gutter-mobile/desktop tokens that already existed. Measured after: h1 left 0->40px at 1440 and 0->16px at 390; elements flush to a viewport edge 30->9 at 390; horizontal overflow unchanged at -5.
findings.title: A second undefined utility strips the gutter off the hero, nav and footer
findings.symptom: At 1440 the headline starts at x=0, hard against the browser edge, while every section below is inset 170-311px. At 390 the headline, body copy, CTAs and cards all touch both screen edges. It reads as unstyled.
findings.cause: web/src/components/AnonymousLanding.jsx uses `px-container-padding` 6 times — hero :573, nav :508, footer :667. The utility `container-padding` is defined nowhere: not in web/src/index.css, not in a tailwind config, and it does not appear in the built CSS. It compiles to nothing.
findings.evidence: Hero <section> computed padding 0px/0px with max-width 1440px; H1 left=0; H2 'What you actually get' left=170; H2 'Three steps' left=311. At 390px: h1 left=0 and 30 elements flush to a viewport edge.
findings.cost: First impression on the highest-traffic screen, and worst on the device most students use.
findings.fix: Same class of bug as F-15 — an undefined token. Define it, or use the px-4 sm:px-6 pattern already present at AnonymousLanding.jsx:295.
findings.pattern_note: F-04 and F-15 are the same root cause twice: a Tailwind utility invented in JSX that was never defined in the theme. Worth a lint rule.

findings.title: The consent checkbox is 16px and most of its label navigates away instead of ticking it
findings.symptom: At the last gate before account creation, clicking the words 'I agree to the Terms of Service' opens the Terms instead of agreeing. The URL becomes /?signup=1#/terms and the box stays unchecked, so 'Create account' stays disabled with no explanation.
findings.cause: web/src/components/AuthModal.jsx:813-831. The checkbox is w-4 h-4 (16px). Its <label htmlFor> contains two <a> elements that call e.stopPropagation() — which correctly stops the toggle but does not stop the anchor navigating.
findings.evidence: Measured: checkbox 16x16px; label 254x14px; the two links occupy 33% and 27% of the label width — 60% of the label does the wrong thing. Reproduced: clicking the label navigated to #/terms with consentChecked=false.
findings.cost: This is the final step of signup. A user who cannot tick the box cannot create an account, and nothing on screen says why the button is dead.
findings.fix: Separate the affordances: make the whole row a 44px hit area that toggles, and move the Terms/Privacy links out of the label (or render them as buttons opening the modal, outside the <label>). Also explain the disabled button.

findings.title: /assignments serves raw JSON instead of the app
findings.symptom: Navigating to /assignments renders the literal text {"detail":"Not authenticated: valid session token required"} on a blank page. No title, no shell, no way back.
findings.cause: server/assignments.py:72 registers @router.get("/assignments") with no /api prefix, shadowing the SPA catch-all. FastAPI matches it before serve_spa_frontend runs.
findings.evidence: HTTP 401 from the live site; document.title empty; body is the JSON error; 1 console error.
findings.fix: Drop the bare /assignments aliases (keep the /api/ ones) and add /assignments to VIEW_PATH_MAP in web/src/App.jsx.
findings.brief_correction: docs/UI_UX_SWEEP.md §3 lists this as SETTLED. It is half-fixed: it stopped returning data and started returning a JSON 401. The alias still shadows the SPA.

findings.title: An API outage silently logs the user out and destroys the session indicator
findings.symptom: With /api/** unreachable, an authenticated visitor is shown the marketing landing page. No error, no spinner, no retry.
findings.cause: web/src/App.jsx:408-484. checkSession() cannot distinguish a transport failure from a 401 — catch(e){} at :428 and :459 swallow both and fall through to the same terminal 'Unauthenticated state' at :464. Then :475-479 deletes localStorage 'token', 'helpotron_csrf_token' and the csrf cookie, so hasSessionIndicator() (web/src/api.js:44) returns false on the NEXT load and the zero-request fast path skips the probe entirely.
findings.aggravating: The offline banner that would explain this is unreachable by construction: it renders inside AppShell (web/src/App.jsx:858), which only mounts when authStatus === 'authed'. The /api/health probe at :288-301 flips `connected`, but nothing renders it in the signedOut branch.
findings.fix: Give checkSession a third outcome. A 401 means signedOut; a network error or 5xx means 'degraded'. Render the shell with an explicit offline state and retry, and never clear the session indicator on a transport failure.

findings.title: Async surfaces are missing their idle / loading / success / error states
findings.symptom: Owner: 'the whole ui/ux is missing alot of idle states, loading states, success states, and error states, everything needs it'.
observed_so_far: Signup submit: the button label vanishes during the request, leaving a bare spinner with no text (measured buttonText='' 1.2s after click).
web/src/App.jsx:81-87 ViewSuspenseFallback is a centred 'Loading…' string — not a skeleton of the view being loaded.
web/src/App.jsx:777 reuses SessionBootScreen ('Checking session…') as the AppShell chunk fallback, so the copy describes the wrong wait.
An assignment created via API sits in pending_approval and appears in no view (brief defect 5) — the success state of a create action is absent entirely.
findings.plan: Enumerate every async surface, record which of the four states exist today, and treat the missing ones as the single largest Stage 2 workstream. This is a system-level fix (one shared set of skeleton/empty/error primitives), not per-screen patches.
findings.note: This is also the brief's own quality bar: 'Every async surface has four designed states.'

findings.title: The only serious axe violation: a 2.57:1 button on the public pricing row
findings.symptom: The 'Apply for free access' button (Testing plan) rendered dark green text on a medium green fill.
findings.cause: web/src/index.css:83, inside :root (the dark theme that is live), paired --st-sem-deepgreen #059669 with --st-on-sem-deepgreen #064E3B. The [data-theme="light"] block at :248 had the correct pairing (#ECFDF5 on #047857) — the two blocks had their foregrounds the wrong way round.
findings.evidence: axe measured 2.57:1 against a 4.5:1 requirement, identically on /, /signup and /guide.
findings.fix_applied: Aligned :root to #ECFDF5 on #047857 = 5.21:1, computed not guessed. First attempt changed only the foreground and reached 3.57:1 — still failing — so the fill was darkened too.
findings.note: I had flagged this from the first landing screenshot as 'green on green'. The number is what made it actionable.

findings.title: Every authenticated page had nested main landmarks
findings.cause: web/index.html:54 mounted React into <main id="root"> while web/src/components/AppShell.jsx:545 renders its own <main id="main-content"> inside it.
findings.fix_applied: Root is now a div; AnonymousLanding's outer element (which already carried id="main-content", the skip-link target) became the <main> for the signed-out side.
findings.honest_note: My first attempt changed index.html alone and REGRESSED the landing page — it was left with no main landmark at all, which axe reported as landmark-one-main plus 42 'region' violations. Caught by re-running axe against the deployed site rather than assuming. Fixed in the same pass before reporting.
findings.lesson: Verify a11y fixes against the deployed page, not the diff.

findings.title: Empty-state copy is written in machine language, not student language
findings.symptom: Opening an empty subject shows: a chip reading 'SUB-PIPELINE 00 · DORMANT', the heading 'No assignments in Mathematics yet', and the instruction 'Import course materials, paste a syllabus link, or launch an agent research thread to activate synthesis vectors.'
findings.cost: This is the screen a new user reaches first, and it is where they must take an action. 'Activate synthesis vectors' and 'SUB-PIPELINE 00 · DORMANT' tell a student nothing about what to do. The heading and the button ('Import Assignment') are fine; the sentence between them is not.
findings.fix: Rewrite in the user's words and run check-comprehension on every empty state. The Assignment Dump empty state (F-23) is already written correctly and is the model.
findings.note: The product vocabulary that must be KEPT is: subject bubble, assignment, Data Lake, Library, Insights, credits, Study Buddy. 'Synthesis vectors' and 'sub-pipeline' are not in that list.

findings.title: The in-app back button is disabled after drilling into a subject
findings.symptom: Opening a subject from the dashboard grid leaves both 'Navigate back' and 'Navigate forward' disabled, so the chrome offers no way back to the grid.
findings.cause: The subject drill-down does not call recordNav (web/src/App.jsx:601), so the back stack stays empty. The URL does not change either (F-07), so the browser's own back button is equally useless.
findings.mitigation_present: An 'All subjects' control exists inside the view, so the user is not trapped — but the global back affordance is visibly present and dead.
findings.fix: Record the navigation, and push a URL for it.

findings.title: Not one skeleton exists in the product — every authed route is the same full-screen spinner
findings.symptom: All 11 authenticated routes sampled 350ms after navigation produced a byte-identical early DOM: the text 'Skip to main content helpotron ACADEMIC OS Checking session…', 0 skeletons, 1 spinner.
findings.evidence: Measured across /dashboard /agent /dump /library /insights /credits /settings /datalake /activity /extension /automation. skeletons:0 on every one. The only loading affordances in the product are web/src/App.jsx:173 SessionBootScreen and :81 ViewSuspenseFallback ('Loading…' as a centred string).
findings.cost: Every view entry looks like a cold boot. The copy also lies after auth resolves, because :777 reuses the session screen as the chunk fallback.
findings.fix: One shared skeleton primitive matching each view's real layout, and separate the 'resolving session' screen from the 'loading this view' screen.

findings.title: Eight of eleven authed routes render two h1 elements
findings.symptom: The breadcrumb emits an h1 for the view name and the view emits its own h1 for its title.
findings.evidence: /agent ['My Agent','current chat'], /dump ['Assignment Dump','Universal Assignment Dump'], /library ['Library','Library & Study Tools'], /insights ['Insights','Cognitive Insights'], /credits ['Billing','Credits & Billing'], /settings ['Settings','Settings & Preferences'], /extension ['Extension','Helpotron Companion Extension'], and /datalake which emits the SAME text twice: ['Data Lake','Data Lake'].
findings.cost: Document-outline violation on most of the product; screen-reader users hear the page title twice.
findings.fix: The breadcrumb is navigation, not a heading — demote it to a span/nav and leave one h1 per view.
findings.related: On /dump there are also two separate breadcrumb trails on one screen: 'Helpotron / Assignment Dump' in the chrome and 'Workspace Core / Assignment Dump / TASK INTAKE' in the content.

findings.title: /activity and /automation do not render their own views
findings.symptom: Both routes render h1 'Dashboard' with ~470-500 characters of body text, where every other view renders 700-5000.
findings.evidence: /activity textLen 501, h1 ['Dashboard']. /automation textLen 467, h1 ['Dashboard']. Both are mapped in web/src/App.jsx VIEW_PATH_MAP (:331, :332) to 'activity' and 'automation'.
findings.brief_correction: Brief defect 8 says '/automation has no h1'. It has one — it is the dashboard's. The real defect is that the view does not render.
findings.fix: Determine whether ActivityView and AutomationCenter are wired at all; either implement or remove the routes.

findings.title: A permanent red 'Low Token Balance' nag on every screen of a freshly funded account
findings.symptom: Immediately after granting the QA account 2,000 tokens, every one of the 11 authed routes showed 'Low Token Balance: You have 2,000 task tokens remaining. View plans →' as a red banner above the content.
findings.cause: web/src/App.jsx:809 computes planLimit from { trial, testing, basic, pro, unlimited }[userPlan] || 15000. New accounts are created with plan='none' (server/main.py:1379), which is not a key in that map, so every such user is measured against the trial allowance. 2000/15000 = 13.3%, under the 15% threshold at :811.
findings.cost: Any plan-'none' user holding under 2,250 tokens is permanently told they are low, on every screen, with a buy-now CTA. It is the loudest element on the page and it is wrong.
findings.fix: Give 'none' an entry (or derive the limit from the account's actual allowance), and make the banner dismissible.

findings.title: The Assignment Dump surface already does three of the four states properly
findings.detail: Pasting an assignment and pressing Upload Text produced: the button disabling immediately, a spinner, a success toast 'Pasted assignment text uploaded!', the counter moving 'Showing 0 of 0 items' -> 'Showing 1 of 1 items', the empty state being replaced, and zero console errors. Round trip ~2.5s via POST /api/dump/upload.
findings.gap: The disabled button keeps the label 'Upload Text' rather than 'Uploading…', so the only progress signal is the spinner.
findings.why_recorded: This is the pattern the rest of the product should copy. The empty state here ('No assignment items in queue' + what to do about it) is also already correct.

findings.status: brief defect 5 does NOT reproduce via the UI path
findings.title: A pasted assignment DID appear on the dashboard
findings.detail: The uploaded item came back from /api/dump/list with status 'auto_routed', and the dashboard then showed '1 assignment present' on one subject card (five others still read '0 assignments present').
findings.caveat: The brief's defect 5 concerns an assignment created through the API, which is a different path and still untested. Also, all six subject cards still show '0 ACTIVE' chips, and the assignment's title is not surfaced on the card.
findings.action: Re-test the API-created path before closing brief defect 5.

findings.title: Cookie consent weights 'ACCEPT ALL' above 'Necessary only'
findings.symptom: The signed-out cookie banner renders 'ACCEPT ALL' as a filled accent button and 'Necessary only' as a quiet outline.
findings.cost: Unequal prominence on a consent choice is the pattern regulators single out, and this product's own copy leans on its privacy posture ('never sell student data', FERPA COMPLIANT chip right there in the banner).
findings.fix: Give both choices the same visual weight.

findings.title: An admin broadcast covers the top-right controls on first load of the dashboard
findings.detail: AdminNoticePopup (web/src/App.jsx:779) opens over the header on entry, overlapping the account and notification controls until dismissed with 'Got it'.
findings.cost: The first thing a new user sees on their first screen is a changelog about a redesign they have no memory of.

findings.title: Signup asked for a discount code before the account existed
findings.symptom: Owner: 'it shouldnt ask for a discount code on signup only on purchase'. The signup form carried an expandable 'Discount code (optional)' field.
findings.worse_than_cosmetic: web/src/components/AuthModal.jsx:298-317 redeemed the code AFTER creating the account. An unrecognised code bounced the user to the sign-in tab with the message 'Account created — discount code not recognized. Sign in to continue.' — so a typo in an optional field ended the signup flow on an error, with the account already made.
findings.fix: Removed the field, its state, and the post-creation redemption branch. Redemption still exists post-signup at Credits → Earn (web/src/components/ReferralSection.jsx:115 → api.redeemReferralCode), so no capability was lost.
findings.verified: Build succeeds; the string 'Discount code (optional)' is absent from the bundle.

findings.title: Every route shares one document title, and it names a different product
findings.symptom: All 15 routes tested report 'Clarion — Study Workspace, Assignment Workflow & Style Coaching'. The product is called Helpotron everywhere else.
findings.cause: web/index.html:9 is the only title in the app. grep for document.title across web/src returns zero matches.
findings.fix: Set a per-view title where activeView changes (web/src/App.jsx:628 handleSelectView) and correct the base title.
findings.brief_correction: Brief defect 6 understates it: the single title is also the wrong brand.

findings.title: /help renders the app's 404
findings.cause: web/src/App.jsx:313-341 VIEW_PATH_MAP has no '/help' entry and PUBLIC_PATHS (:343) does not contain it, so resolvePath falls to setNotFoundPath at :358. A Guide view exists and /guide works.
findings.evidence: HTTP 200, renders 'NOT FOUND · 404 Page not found'. The footer's own 'Help Center' control points here.
findings.fix: Map '/help' to the guide view, or redirect server-side like /login.

findings.title: Authenticated navigation never changes the URL — nothing inside the app is shareable
findings.cause: web/src/App.jsx:628 handleSelectView sets React state only. The only history calls are replaceState (:380, :385, :501). pushState appears solely in AnonymousLanding.jsx (:422-453), the signed-out marketing nav.
findings.cost: No bookmarking, sharing, or browser back/forward — the app ships its own back/forward stack (:606-624) to compensate.
findings.fix: pushState in handleSelectView using VIEW_PATH_MAP in reverse, and handle popstate.

findings.title: Marketing nav links are cosmetic — /features and /pricing are byte-identical to /
findings.cause: web/src/App.jsx:343 PUBLIC_PATHS includes both, so resolvePath returns early (:352) and AnonymousLanding renders unchanged. The sections have ids (#features :624, #pricing :295) but the path never triggers a scroll.
findings.cost: A visitor who clicks Pricing lands at the top of a 5271px page and must hunt.
findings.brief_correction: Brief defect 8 says '/features has no h1'. It has one — it IS the landing page. That half is stale.

findings.title: Nav and footer controls are 16px tall on desktop
findings.evidence: Measured at 1440: 9 controls under the 32px desktop floor (Features 55x16, Guide 37x16, Pricing 44x16, Sign in 43x16, Privacy Policy 89x16, Terms 107x16, Help Center 75x16, Extension Companion 162x20).
findings.correction: My first pass reported these as failing the 44px TOUCH floor at 390px. That was an artefact of measuring in a desktop browser at a narrow width. web/src/index.css:573-577 applies min-height/min-width 44px inside @media (pointer: coarse), so a real phone DOES get 44px targets. The defect is real on desktop (16px vs the 32px floor) and on any fine-pointer device; it is NOT a touch failure.
findings.fix: Give the nav and footer controls padding so the hit area is >=32px regardless of pointer type; the label size can stay.

findings.title: Guide, Terms, Privacy and Extension are modals wearing URLs, and each puts two h1s on the page
findings.evidence: /guide h1s = ['Your Academic Co-pilot, Redefined', 'Helpotron Field Guide'], modalOpen true. Same for /terms, /privacy, /extension.
findings.fix: Demote the landing h1 on these paths, or render them as real pages.

findings.title: The brand logo is a 36px JPEG
findings.cause: Two load /HelpoTron_logo.jpeg at 36x36 and 24x24. A lossy raster with no transparency on a near-black ground. An SVG AnimatedLogo already exists and is imported at web/src/App.jsx:25.
findings.note: Not a breach of the no-AI-imagery rule — a real brand asset — but it is the only raster in the product.

findings.title: The skip link measures 1x1px until focused
findings.detail: web/src/App.jsx:714-719, sr-only + focus:not-sr-only. Correct pattern; recorded so it is not re-counted against the tap-target metric.

findings.status: stale — brief defect does not reproduce
findings.title: The 1.5-3s landing flash on authenticated hard loads appears already fixed
findings.detail: web/src/App.jsx:206 initialises authStatus synchronously and :767 renders SessionBootScreen while 'checking'. AnonymousLanding renders only on 'signedOut' (:769), so the marketing page cannot paint during a session probe.
findings.residual: Weaker but real: the boot screen is a full-screen spinner rather than a shell skeleton, and :777 reuses it as the AppShell chunk fallback so the copy lies. The 1200ms retry at :439 adds a second of spinner in the cookie-race case. Folded into F-18.
findings.brief_correction: Re-scope defect 2 from 'landing page flash' to 'no skeleton, and the fallback copy is wrong'.

findings.title: Turnstile in managed mode did not stop scripted account creation
findings.detail: The QA account was created through the real UI with no bypass header. Turnstile issued a 730-char token after ~6-12s with no interactive challenge, because the client is real Chrome with a real TLS fingerprint on a residential IP. Plain curl requests to the site also returned 200 without challenge.
findings.implication: Turnstile raises the cost of automation; it is not a wall. If the signup rate limit (20/hour per IP, server/main.py:1332) is the real control, that is worth knowing explicitly.
findings.not_a_recommendation_to_change: Recorded as a fact about the current posture, not a request to tighten it.

still_to_verify: Consent gate (brief defect 3): confirmed live on screen ('STEP 2 OF 2 · CONFIRM CONSENT') and localStorage-scoped at App.jsx:400-406/588 — still need what renders behind it and the new-browser repeat
pending_approval assignments invisible in the UI (brief defect 5)
Rate limits under ordinary use (brief defect 7)
axe / pa11y violation counts per route
The full authed walk: subject -> assignment dump -> generate -> history -> library -> insights -> credits -> settings -> API keys -> export

summary.reading_order: work open_ids by severity: critical -> high -> medium -> low. F-23 is the positive reference pattern; do not change it.

field_notes.status: original free-text status from the outgoing agent — kept verbatim
field_notes.brief_correction: present where the original brief was wrong about this finding
